instrument.title: Diplomatic Appointments (Selection Process) Bill 2026
instrument.stage: Senate: presented and read a first time on 7 September 2026 (private Senator's Bill, Senator Payman); later Senate stages not known, because aph.gov.au and ParlInfo refused scripted access on 2026-10-02. House of Representatives: not yet before the House. Not passed by either House.

scope.in: the whole Bill: ss 1-16, all Parts
out: s 3 (Simplified outline of this Act) as a source of rules: it is read and kept as text, and set against the operative provisions (category X), but not encoded as rules, because a simplified outline is not intended to be operative (OPC Drafting Direction 1.3A, item cth-opc-dd-1-3a)

column 3 of the commencement table in s 2(1), the table of contents, the long title, and the notes to s 2(1) and s 10(7): not part of the operative law (s 2(2) for column 3); the notes are read for category X and F, not encoded
the content of any rules made under s 16, and offices prescribed under s 7(2): none have been made, since the Bill is not law; the encoding takes 'prescribed by the rules' as an input

the State and Territory laws under which ministerial and opposition staff are employed (s 8(2)(c)), and the membership laws of State and Territory legislatures (s 8(1), (2)(a)): eight jurisdictions' laws; whether a person was a member or such an employee is taken as a fact

international law that the Bill's subject matter engages but the Bill does not cite: the Vienna Conventions on Diplomatic Relations (agrement, art 4; charge d'affaires ad interim, art 19) and on Consular Relations; recorded in the reference register as out of scope
scope.why: The Bill is short (16 sections) and every operative section bears on the outcome it regulates, whether an appointment to a designated diplomatic office may be made, must be terminated, or needs a Selection Committee, so nothing operative is left out. What is left out is either not operative (the outline, notes, column 3) or law outside the Commonwealth Bill whose result the Bill only reads as a fact (State and Territory staffing and membership, international conventions), where encoding it would cost much and decide nothing the Bill decides. The human approves or changes this at 3H.
